newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Exxon inaugurates first China joint venture - source.
newsitem.headline: Exxon inaugurates first China joint venture - source.

text.p: Exxon Chemical Eastern Company Inc inaugurated a joint-venture lubricants plant in China on Tuesday with state-owned Sinopec Jinzhou Petrochemical Co, an Exxon statement said.
Both companies have a 50-percent stake in the Jinzhou Jinex Lubricant Additives Co Ltd which was formed in 1995. The joint venture is Exxon's first in China, an Exxon source said.
The company source said the feedstock for the joint venture's lubricant plant would be sourced both domestically and through imports.
Its production of lubricants additives, including detergent inhibitor packages and viscosity modifiers, was aimed primarily for the domestic Chinese market, the source said.
The source could not reveal either the cost or the size of the plant.
The plant which came onstream as scheduled in September, is located in Jinzhou in the north-eastern province of Liao Ning where Sinopec Jinzhou Petrochemical has a major petrochemical complex.
The Chinese state petrochemical company is among China's largest manufacturers of lubricant additive components with an extensive domestic marketing network.

Exxon which has a 130,000 tonnes-per-year additives plant in Singapore and smaller plants in Australia and Japan, signed a non-binding letter of intent with Anglo-Dutch major Shell in July to form a joint venture petroleum and additives company which they hope to start up in 1997.
